title: Framework Engineering Boundary Discrimination Pilot
question: Can an evaluator distinguish a non-redundant Framework Engineering scope from adjacent method engineering and generic structured analysis using only current canonical claims?
claim_under_test: Framework Engineering has a defensible boundary that is not fully subsumed by adjacent disciplines or generic structured analysis.
objective: Pilot the experiment infrastructure while producing an adversarial boundary assessment useful for preregistering FE-MISSION-001.
evaluator_role: You are a blinded, adversarial research-method evaluator. Your goal is discrimination accuracy, not preservation of Framework Engineering terminology.
assumptions: The selected repository records accurately represent the current provisional position.
confounders: Language models may share training priors
No primary standards corpus is included in this low-cost pilot
procedure: Extract only mechanisms, scope constraints, and claimed outcomes stated in the permitted inputs.
Construct the strongest plausible subsumption account under method engineering or generic structured analysis.
Identify candidate non-redundant mechanisms and test whether each is definitional, operational, and evidenced.
Classify the boundary as distinguishable, partially distinguishable, fully subsumed, or inconclusive.
Recommend evidence needed for a decisive FE-MISSION-001 protocol without updating canonical theory.
replication_plan: Use at least two independent evaluators from different provider families or one provider plus a human reviewer. Do not reveal earlier results.
falsification_conditions: Every claimed FE mechanism maps to an adjacent or generic practice without loss of scope or predicted outcome.
Candidate distinctions are vocabulary-only or rely on unsupported discipline claims.
inconclusive_conditions: Permitted inputs lack operational detail needed to compare mechanisms.
stopping_conditions: Stop if any requested input is missing or if independent-result isolation cannot be maintained.
synthesis_policy: No confidence update from model agreement alone. Synthesis may refine the FE-MISSION-001 protocol but cannot accept or reject FEH-001.
adjudication_policy: Resolve factual disputes through cited repository evidence or later primary-source review; do not use majority vote.
privacy_and_security: Only declared public repository inputs may be sent to an external provider.
cost_and_resource_limits: At most one trial per provider in the pilot; external execution requires explicit --execute.
